prove_sample.question: can a bounded agent prove the label of a random row?
prove_sample.frame: solutions/, no proof in solutions-proved/, non-empty label
prove_sample.note_on_contradiction: Every proof in these campaigns is an upper bound. A bound ABOVE the label is `looser` -- it fails to confirm the label and cannot disagree with it, since that needs a lower bound. A bound BELOW the label does bear on it, but only after the other two explanations are ruled out: `tighter-costmodel` (the charge table costs something CPython does not) and `tighter-translation` (the Dafny runs a cheaper algorithm than the Python).

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: real-number tuple-sort quantifiers combined with a nonlinear Pow2 bound. The agent also suspects the true charged cost is quadratic, but never closed a proof, so that suspicion is not evidence.
rows.why_failed: Solve mixes real-number tuple-sort quantifiers (forall x in ratios/d) with the new nonlinear Pow2Cost/SortCost step arithmetic in one VC; Z3 does not close it even at 3x the time budget. Note: the real obstacle here is more than proof technique -- Pow2_140 is linear recursion (not squaring), so this row's true charged cost is O(n^2), genuinely disagreeing with its O(nlogn) label, but that disagreement was never machine-checked because the surrounding VC would not close.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: the chained bound needs three multiplication facts at once; isolating each did not close the chain.
rows.why_failed: the final chained bound needs each multiplication (SortCost(|c|)<=..., |c|<=2|s|, CeilLog2 monotonicity) isolated into its own lemma the way solutions-proved/nlogn/603_284 does; combining them in inline asserts made the nonlinear arithmetic too much for Z3 within the time limit

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: the proved cost contains a binary search over the VALUE a*b, not over the query count. Whether a loop bounded by a capped value counts as constant is the open value-versus-size convention.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: merge sort charged with the loose O(k^2) scaffold; the agent states the tight O(k log k) bound was not attempted. Nothing here bears on the label.

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: proves 6*|numbers|*MaxLen(numbers)+... because comparing a string against a running best costs per-character. Whether string length is a size parameter is the same open convention.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: SortCost/CeilLog2 bound verifies standalone; times out combined with the SumSizes additive term in one VC.
rows.why_failed: Z3 cannot combine the SortCost/CeilLog2 nonlinear recursion-tree bound with the additive SumSizes(ans-length) threading in Solve's single verification condition; the two arguments verify individually but not together within the time limit, and the opaque/{:opaque}+reveal split that fixed the same timeout in 2188_359 and 2426_4 was not tried before the budget ran out.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: same sort scaffold as 1421_89. Proof slack, not a label finding.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: sort bound verifies as a standalone lemma; the surrounding method's VC does not close in 30s.
rows.why_failed: even with the sort's own nonlinear bound isolated and verified as a standalone lemma, the surrounding method (two flag loops + two RemoveFirst charges + branch merge) still made the combined postcondition VC too large for Z3 in 30s; needs the whole linear+log combination split into one more helper lemma taking the raw steps arithmetic out of the method body

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.relation_reason: quadratic base bound plus a further (n+2)*idx term would not combine into the n^2 postcondition.
rows.why_failed: the postcondition needs base1 (itself a quadratic-in-n bound) combined with a further (n+2)*idx term to prove <= a single n^2 coefficient; Z3 won't do this nonlinear combination without isolated MulMonoRight/MulDistrib-style lemmas, which weren't written before the budget ran out.

rows.label: O(1)
rows.relation_reason: the invariant mechanism was found; it ran out of its 3 attempts one edit short of the final case split. Expected to close with more budget.
rows.why_failed: needed one more edit (an explicit if/else on hitFound after the inner loop to select the right half of the split invariant) -- the mechanism is right, just short one attempt

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: square-monotonicity (a<=b ==> a*a<=b*b) would not discharge even isolated.
rows.why_failed: Z3 would not close a square-monotonicity lemma (a<=b ==> a*a<=b*b) needed to lift SortCost's per-element O(k^2) bound to a bound in terms of n; combined with this row's pre-existing per-index exists/forall invariants, Solve times out at 30s independent of that lemma.

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.bound: 4*|data_list|*|data_list| + 20*|data_list| + 3*r_final + 6*span_total + 20, where r_final is the stabilized r and span_total is an exact ghost sum of the inner while's true per-neg-element trip counts
rows.relation_reason: PROVED 2026-09-17 once the convention made r an available parameter. Bound 4*|data_list|^2 + 20*|data_list| + 3*r_final + 6*span_total + 20: the n^2 term matches the label, the r and span terms are value-derived and the label omits them.

rows.label: O(n)
rows.bound: 40 * n + 3 * SumFirst(pairs, n) + 4, where SumFirst sums each test case's own n-value

rows.label: O(1)
rows.relation_reason: IntToString costs the digit count of n, i.e. log of the value. Constant only if the value is treated as capped.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: isolating the |arr| vs |pairs|+1 substitution into its own lemma did not help.
rows.why_failed: even isolating the |arr| vs |pairs|+1 substitution into its own trivial lemma didn't help -- the timeout is at the whole-method VC, suggesting Z3 retries nonlinear search across the combined SortCost unfolding + CeilLog2 + linear steps terms together rather than at any one identified step; would need the whole postcondition's arithmetic moved into one dedicated closing lemma taking steps as a parameter

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: the third loop's range comes from input values with no requires tying it to n, so the bound carries 4*max(0, hi-lo) beyond the linear term.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: same sort scaffold as 1421_89. Proof slack, not a label finding.

rows.label: O(n*m)
rows.relation_reason: PROVED 2026-09-17. Bound 4050*(if n>0 then n else 0)+5. m is the LITERAL 2009 in the source, not an input, so it cannot scale and folds into the constant. The row is O(n) and the O(n*m) label overstates it. This is a strictly tighter bound than the label, which is the one way an upper bound can refute one. A literal is not the value-versus-size case: that convention governs quantities that vary with input.

prove_sample_2.note_on_contradiction: Every proof in these campaigns is an upper bound. A bound ABOVE the label is `looser` -- it fails to confirm the label and cannot disagree with it, since that needs a lower bound. A bound BELOW the label does bear on it, but only after the other two explanations are ruled out: `tighter-costmodel` (the charge table costs something CPython does not) and `tighter-translation` (the Dafny runs a cheaper algorithm than the Python).

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: amortized: sum of per-iteration Log2Floor costs telescopes because nn decreases by exactly the returned power each outer iteration

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.why_failed: the loop is `decreases *` in the original (unproven termination); a ghost step bound needs a digit-growth convergence argument relating pow=9**i to NumDigits(nn) that was not attempted given the risk/budget tradeoff

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.why_failed: combining the O(n**2) step accounting with the pre-existing forall-membership invariants pushed verification over the 30s limit

rows.label: O(n)
rows.why_failed: Dfs's recursion depth depends on how fast x shrinks against a quadratically-spaced lookup table (FindIdxFrom); bounding that depth is a real number-theoretic argument, not fitting the budget

rows.label: O(n+m)log(n+m)
rows.relation_reason: Sort charged via quadratic SortCost scaffold (Sort/Merge live in prelude.dfy, off limits); did not attempt the CeilLog2 recursion-tree tight bound.

rows.label: O(nlogn+mlogm)
rows.relation_reason: Python compares sorted(g1) != sorted(g2), which is the source of the nlogn+mlogm label. The Dafny compares multiset(s1) != multiset(s2), charged |s1|+|s2| by the cost table, and the proved bound is linear. Same output, cheaper algorithm: the proof bears on the translation, not on the label.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.why_failed: substring-scan cost (Contains1272b) adds a SumLen(arr) term whose prefix bookkeeping did not close, and the shared SortCost nlogn lemma timed out once combined with that extra machinery

rows.label: O(logn)
rows.why_failed: the pos/level-advance loop's per-step increase in n is not bounded by a constant, so the standard decreases-metric-bounds-iteration-count argument gives itnAdv<=initM+overshoot, not itnAdv<=initM; closing it needs a separate bound on the overshoot that was not found in budget

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.why_failed: post-loop step bound (steps<=base2+4*(n-1)) would not close after the second while loop even though the loop invariant steps<=base2+4*i verified inside the loop

rows.label: O(n)
rows.relation_reason: Gcd charged as O(1) int arithmetic per call, consistent with the stipulated table

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.why_failed: hit the 5-minute wall while fixing a nat-subtraction typing error (steps-base1 not proved nonnegative) after resolving the earlier Z3 timeout

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: two sorts of disjoint sub-lists bounded by N via a combined SortCost lemma

rows.label: O(n)
rows.why_failed: CeilSqrt's binary search over the VALUE numbers[i] (not the list length) needs its own charged bound; getting the two nested loops' step counts to compose into a single proved formula in x did not close in 3 attempts. Real cost is O(log v) per element, a per-element cost the O(n) label omits (would have been looser-structural).

rows.label: O(logn)
rows.why_failed: second-loop invariant res>=b0*Pow2Aux(cnt2) would not re-establish after res:=res*k; needed one more isolated associativity lemma than the budget allowed

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.why_failed: Z3 would not connect base1/base3 chained nonlinear bounds to the final n**2 ensures even after isolating each multiplication into its own lemma call

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: SortInts charged via quadratic SortCost scaffold (Sort lives in prelude.dfy, off limits); did not attempt the tight CeilLog2 recursion-tree bound.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.relation_reason: SortInts charged via quadratic SortCost scaffold (Sort lives in prelude.dfy, off limits); did not attempt the tight CeilLog2 recursion-tree bound.

rows.label: O(nlogn)
rows.why_failed: the scan loop initializes i:=1 before checking n, so an invariant bounding i by n is false on entry whenever n==0; needs a case split or an i<=n+1-style invariant not yet found

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.relation_reason: fact(n) loops over the input value n, so the proved bound 2*AbsInt(i)+4 is linear in that value. The O(n**2) label comes from CPython's bignum multiplication, whose cost grows with the operands' digit count; COMPLEXITY.md charges every int operation 1. The gap is the stipulated cost model.

rows.label: O(n)
rows.why_failed: row keeps `decreases *` on an unbounded stack-based BFS traversal; a real bound needs a potential-function argument (total pushes bounded by sum of vertex degrees over a tree) that the 5-minute budget cannot fit, and the rule against decreases * would also have to be resolved as part of the same proof

rows.label: O(n**2)
rows.why_failed: the classic sieve inner while (step size i, bound 2000) needs itn*i=j-j0 to cap iterations, which is nonlinear in the two ghost/loop variables and did not close in budget; the n*n tail loop was never reached for instrumentation
